actual_scope: For the selected pair-0 stage-0 forward / stage-1 backward boundary, enumerate every directed coordinate transvection T_ij = I + E_ij on the 9-coordinate port frames and screen the most favorable rank-one transition invoice.
scope_change_reason: The task card asks for an actual two-call boundary mechanism. This run fixes that boundary and tests one concrete rank-one map family, all 72 directed coordinate shears, across all 112 ports; it does not claim a legal scalar composition.
bottleneck_link: A single shared boundary map could remove repeated rank-one transitions; the exact census tests whether that map exists, and the selected-profile screen measures the best charged count-only case.
stop_rule: Enumerate all 72 coordinate transvections for each of the 112 pinned port pairs, then stop if there is no common map and the one-shear/two-transition profile does not lower the selected ceiling.
evidence: Every port has 6 or 42 compatible shears (77 and 35 ports, respectively; 1,932 incidences total), but the common set is empty. Under the optimistic invoice of one rank-one shear paid and two rank-one boundary transitions removed per port, the selected local rank-one profile changes from 2,412 to 21,701/9 per call. The exact a-ceiling rises from 1690054109089/10^15 to 338060003381/200000000000000, a 0.01455% increase; this weakens the profile-only bound. Full scalar endpoints, legal composition, and supplier integration are unverified, so no new kappa is claimed.
